'''Antony John Wassermann''' (born 1957) is a British mathematician working in [[operator algebras]]. He is known for his works on [[conformal field theory]] (providing several series of [[subfactor]]s), the actions of [[compact group]]s on [[von Neumann algebras]], and his proof of the [[Baum–Connes conjecture]] for connected [[reductive group|reductive linear Lie groups]].<ref name="Whi">[https://doi.org/10.1112/blms/23.1.109 Two paragraphs citation for the Junior Whitehead Prize, published in the Bull. London Math. Soc., January 1991]</ref><ref>[[Vaughan Jones]] published a [http://www.numdam.org/item/SB_1994-1995__37__251_0.pdf report in the 1994 Seminaire Bourbaki no. 800]</ref>

== Biography ==
Wassermann was born in 1957.<ref name="DOB" /> He is the son of the quantum physicist Gerhard Dietrich Wassermann and the brother of the mathematician Alexander Simon Wassermann.<ref>[https://www.gla.ac.uk/schools/mathematicsstatistics/staff/awassermann Webpage of Simon Wassermann]</ref> He was educated at the [[Royal Grammar School, Newcastle upon Tyne]], and [[St John's College, Cambridge]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Cambridge tripos results: Science and mathematics |work=The Times |date=28 June 1976 |page=17}}</ref> before going on to earn his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] from the [[University of Pennsylvania]] in 1981 under the supervision of [[Jonathan Rosenberg (mathematician)|Jonathan Rosenberg]]. His doctoral dissertation was titled, "Automorphic actions of compact groups on operator algebras".<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=23131|name=Antony John Wassermann}}</ref><ref>[https://repository.upenn.edu/dissertations/AAI8127086 PhD Dissertation, University of Pennsylvania, 1981]</ref> Afterwards, he was ''Directeur de Recherches'' of the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]] (CNRS) at [[Aix-Marseille University]] from 1999 to 2013.<ref name="DOB">[https://web.archive.org/web/20110331201826/http://iml.univ-mrs.fr/editions/Rapports/RA2006-2010/RA-2006-2010-projet-2011-2015.pdf Activity report, ''Institut de Mathématiques de Luminy'', page 152]</ref>

== Honours ==
* Bronze medal, [[International Mathematical Olympiad]], 1974.<ref>[https://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=11070 International Mathematical Olympiad]</ref>
* [[Miller Research Fellows]]hip recipient in 1986–88.<ref>The article [https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/1E3A88619EED8E092AA45A0525AAB78F/S0008414X00004028a.pdf/ergodic_actions_of_compact_groups_on_operator_algebras_ii_classification_of_full_multiplicity_ergodic_actions.pdf "Ergodic Actions of Compact Groups on Operator Algebras II"](Canadian Journal of Mathematics, 1988) explicitly mentions on page 1483 the support from the Miller Institute, University of California, Berkeley.</ref>
* Winner of the [[Whitehead Prize]] in 1990.<ref>[https://www.lms.ac.uk/prizes/list-lms-prize-winners#Whead Winners of the Whitehead Prize]</ref><ref name="Whi"/>
* Invited speaker, [[International Congresses of Mathematicians]], 1994, Zürich.<ref>[https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=wassermann Invited speakers, International Congresses of Mathematicians]</ref>

==Selected bibliography==
* ''Operator algebras and conformal field theory. III. Fusion of positive energy representations of LSU(N) using bounded operators.'' Invent. Math. 133, no. 3, 467–538, 1998. [https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet-getitem?mr=1645078 MR1645078]
* ''Operator algebras and conformal field theory.'' Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, Vol. 1, 2 (Zürich, 1994), 966–979, Birkhäuser, Basel, 1995. [https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet-getitem?mr=1403996 MR1403996]
* ''Ergodic actions of compact groups on operator algebras. I. General theory.'' Ann. of Math. (2) 130, no. 2, 273–319, 1989. [https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet-getitem?mr=1014926 MR1014926]
* ''Ergodic actions of compact groups on operator algebras. III.'' Classification for SU(2). Invent. Math. 93, no. 2, 309–354, 1988. [https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet-getitem?mr=948104 MR948104]
* ''Une démonstration de la conjecture de Connes–Kasparov pour les groupes de Lie linéaires connexes réductifs'' [A proof of the Connes–Kasparov conjecture for connected reductive linear Lie groups], C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris Sér. I Math. 304, no. 18, 559–562, 1987. [https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet-getitem?mr=894996 MR894996]
